articles.title: Chennai Entrepreneur's Viral Post Reopens India's Work-Life Balance Debate
articles.excerpt: Sundara Rajan says he worked up to 14-hour days, six-and-a-half days a week, at a construction firm from 1986 to 1994 — needing four hours' permission just for a haircut — reviving the 70-hour workweek debate sparked by Narayana Murthy and L&T's S. N. Subrahmanyan.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals abroad navigate the same hustle-culture expectations — from H-1B tech workers to Gulf engineers — and the Murthy/Subrahmanyan remarks landed in diaspora circles because they capture the tension between pride in the work ethic and its cost in health and family time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Court Orders Swiggy, Restaurant to Pay ₹1 Lakh Over Misleading 'Cost for Two'
articles.excerpt: The North Delhi consumer commission ruled that a "cost for two" figure shown without any disclaimer is a binding price promise — and that Swiggy can't dodge liability behind intermediary safe harbour when it does no price checks.
articles.nri_angle: Swiggy Dineout is widely used by families visiting India to book large restaurant dinners, so the ruling gives NRIs and their relatives the same billing protections as local diners.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Navratri 2026: Sadhguru Says Nine Days of Fasting Are About Awareness, Not Denial
articles.excerpt: Shardiya Navratri begins October 11. Sadhguru frames the nine-day fast as a practice in bodily awareness — with lighter sattvic food, a two-hour gap after meals, and no mandatory restrictions in Isha's 2026 sadhana.
articles.image_caption: An illustration of Goddess Durga with a lion, framed by marigold garlands. Shardiya Navratri 2026 begins on October 11, with nine days of worship devoted to the Divine Feminine.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora communities from the US to the UK mark Navratri with garba nights and Durga pujas, and Isha's free live webstream lets devotees join the celebrations from anywhere.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: How to Time Your Flu Shot and Pick the Right Option This Fall
articles.excerpt: Doctors say October is the sweet spot for most people, with enhanced shots for those 65 and older — and a new mRNA flu vaccine on the market. For travelers to India, the timing question is different.
articles.image_caption: A vaccination record showing the lot number and date of a previous shot; health experts recommend getting this fall's flu shot in September or October.
articles.nri_angle: India saw a sharp H1N1 surge in August and demand for flu vaccines tripled; diaspora members traveling to India face a different flu calendar than the US winter season and should vaccinate well before their trip.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Johns Hopkins Study: Time-Restricted Eating Brings Modest Weight Loss Without Counting Calories
articles.excerpt: A 12-week feeding trial found adults with obesity and prediabetes lost a median 2.7% of body weight on a 10-hour eating window — nearly identical to the control group — while improving eating habits but not inflammation or appetite hormones.
articles.image_caption: Two carrots arranged like clock hands sit on a white plate with a knife and fork. The Johns Hopkins feeding trial found a 10-hour eating window produced modest weight loss nearly identical to the control group.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians develop type 2 diabetes at lower body weights than other populations, so a feeding trial on prediabetes and obesity — finding that an eating window helps habits but the diet itself does the work — is directly relevant to the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gastroenterologist Explains Six Everyday Habits That Cause Bloating After Meals
articles.excerpt: Eating too fast, oversized dinners, hidden constipation and poor sleep — Dr Vineet K Gupta says recurring bloating is usually about repeated daily behaviours, not a single bad food.
articles.image_caption: Gastroenterologists recommend balanced, fibre-rich meals to ease bloating.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian diaspora households eat late, large, lentil-and-bean-heavy dinners — the exact pattern Dr Gupta flags — making his slow-down, track-patterns advice a low-cost starting point before supplements or elimination diets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: From Bachchan to Kher, Bollywood's Veterans Prove Fitness Has No Age Limit
articles.excerpt: At 83, Amitabh Bachchan preaches caring for the body; at 88, Dharmendra mixes gym work with physiotherapy; at 70, Anupam Kher lifts heavy — Bollywood's senior stars are making strength after 70 look normal.
articles.image_caption: Dharmendra poses in a gym wearing a workout shirt and cap. The 88-year-old actor shared the Instagram video to show fans his daily exercise and physiotherapy routine.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs watching aging parents from afar, these stars' public fitness routines offer a conversation starter and a cultural counterweight to the idea that slowing down after 60 is inevitable.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Quitting ultra-processed food may ease depression, small UCSF study finds
articles.excerpt: In a first-of-its-kind 20-person crossover trial published in JAMA Psychiatry, participants who cut ultra-processed food by 85% saw moderate-to-large improvements in depression symptoms.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian diaspora households juggling convenience food get one more evidence point favoring traditional minimally processed home cooking, though the study is preliminary and not medical advice.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Three Indian Employees in Their 30s Has Elevated Blood Sugar
articles.excerpt: Loop Health's Workforce Health Index 2026, built on 816,000+ lab values, found blood-sugar dysfunction rising from 16.7% in employees' 20s to 52.9% in their 40s — with most people unaware anything is wrong.
articles.image_caption: A blood glucose meter used to test blood sugar levels
articles.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated diabetes risk at lower body weights, so an annual HbA1c check in the 30s is a sensible baseline — and diaspora readers can nudge family in India in precisely the urban-workforce cohort this report covers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indore Clinic Launches Madhya Pradesh's First Alzheimer's Blood Biomarker Test
articles.excerpt: Sampurna Sodani Diagnostic Clinic in Indore says its new pTau217 and Aβ42 blood test can flag Alzheimer's-related brain changes 10 to 15 years before symptoms, offering a less invasive alternative to spinal taps and PET scans.
articles.image_caption: An illustration depicts an elderly man with a puzzle-piece brain graphic labeled Alzheimer's Disease. Sampurna Sodani Diagnostic Clinic in Indore says its new pTau217 and A-beta-42 blood biomarker test can flag Alzheimer's-related brain changes 10 to 15 years before symptoms appear.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families with aging parents in India, the test adds a concrete option for elder-care planning back home: a blood-based screening in a tier-2 city can give NRIs coordinating care from abroad an earlier, clearer picture of a parent's cognitive health without requiring travel to a metro hospital.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vaping Harms the Heart Too, Not Just the Lungs, Doctors Warn
articles.excerpt: Growing research shows e-cigarettes expose users to chemicals that damage blood vessels and disrupt heart rhythm — and a new expert consensus says no nicotine product is safe for the heart.
articles.image_caption: An electronic cigarette; doctors warn vaping harms the heart as well as the lungs
articles.nri_angle: Vaping remains widely available to young people despite India's 2019 ban, and diaspora families in the US and UK face aggressive youth marketing of flavored vapes — doctors advise parents to treat vaping as a genuine cardiovascular risk, not a phase.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Should You Get a COVID Shot This Fall? The 2026–27 Vaccines Are Here
articles.excerpt: Four updated vaccines targeting the XFG variant won FDA approval for the 2026–27 season, with eligibility centered on older adults and people with underlying conditions.
articles.image_caption: Vials of COVID-19 vaccine. The FDA has approved four updated shots for the 2026–27 season targeting the XFG variant.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-American households planning fall gatherings and India trips, booking the updated shot weeks before holiday travel gives protection time to build — especially for grandparents and immunocompromised family members.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Konkona Sen Sharma Shares Dengue Recovery Update From Hospital Bed
articles.excerpt: The actor posted a hospital-bed photo on Instagram, told followers she is 'better now,' and was back at Lust Stories 3 promotions by Sunday.
articles.image_caption: Konkona Sen Sharma shared a dengue recovery update from her hospital bed.
articles.nri_angle: Dengue remains a seasonal risk for diaspora travellers visiting India during the monsoon months — a reminder from an unlikely public-health messenger.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Measles-exposed Amtrak traveler rode through six California counties
articles.excerpt: An unvaccinated passenger later hospitalized with measles traveled by train and bus through six counties Sept. 12–14; L.A. Union Station visitors from Saturday 8 a.m.–noon should monitor symptoms through Oct. 3.
articles.image_caption: A close-up shows the red, blotchy measles rash spread across a person’s neck and upper chest. California health officials are warning of measles exposure across six counties after an unvaccinated Amtrak passenger traveled through the state Sept. 12–14.
articles.nri_angle: With Diwali travel weeks away, California's Indian diaspora families — frequent Amtrak and air travelers — should check MMR vaccination status before heading to busy stations or traveling to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: At 81, This Gurugram Grandmother Is Still Travelling, Working — and Fully Confident
articles.excerpt: A viral Instagram video by Gurgaon-based founder Mehar Toor shows her 81-year-old grandmother — a businesswoman fresh off an Alaska cruise — explaining her philosophy in one line: she feels fully confident she can go anywhere.
articles.image_caption: An 81-year-old Gurugram grandmother pictured with her granddaughter, startup founder Mehar Toor. The dadi, a businesswoman and avid traveller, recently returned from an Alaska cruise.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families who track their elders' health across time zones, this dadi flips the script — a gentle challenge to every family that has quietly decided what an 81-year-old can and cannot do.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Raise Your Sum Insured or Buy Riders? How Experts Say to Prioritise
articles.excerpt: A cheap super top-up can take family cover to Rs 1 crore for about Rs 4,500 a year - but riders like consumables cover and critical-illness protection still earn their place. Here is how to prioritise.
articles.image_caption: A hospital exterior. Experts say the ideal target is about ₹1 crore of total health cover, and a super top-up is usually the cheapest way to raise it.
articles.nri_angle: A live question for NRIs insuring aging parents in India: a super top-up is the cheapest way to bring an old Rs 5 lakh policy up to a realistic level.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: PFRDA Finalises NPS Swasthya: 25% Medical Withdrawal Cap, Health Cover Up to Rs 30 Lakh
articles.excerpt: The pension regulator's September 18 guidelines spell out how much NPS Swasthya subscribers can draw for healthcare, the mandatory four-tier family-floater insurance, and what happens if a renewal premium goes unpaid.
articles.nri_angle: India-domestic product; the natural diaspora audience is NRIs planning retirement in India, though NRI eligibility details were not spelled out in the guidelines' published summaries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Irregular Periods, Acne, Hair Thinning: 5 Signs You May Have PMOS
articles.excerpt: A doctor explains the five patterns — from unpredictable cycles to hair thinning — that warrant medical evaluation, and which tests a doctor may recommend.
articles.image_caption: A woman holds a calendar marked with question marks over expected period dates. Unpredictable or missed periods are among the key signs of PMOS that doctors say warrant medical evaluation.
articles.nri_angle: PMOS affects an estimated 1 in 8 women and often goes undiagnosed for years — an awareness gap this explainer addresses for women and families in the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Very Hot Tea and Coffee Triple Esophageal Cancer Risk, Major Study Finds
articles.excerpt: An Oxford analysis of nearly one million adults found the risk comes from heat itself — not tea or coffee — and that letting a drink cool for a few minutes may prevent a meaningful share of cases.
articles.image_caption: A cup of black tea. A new study found drinking very hot tea and coffee can triple esophageal cancer risk.
articles.nri_angle: For chai-drinking households, the study's simple takeaway — let the cup cool a few minutes before sipping — fits naturally into daily routine.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
